author: StefaniaHergane
title: Debian Packages job fails - apt-get cannot resolve archive.ubuntu.com mirrors (DNS resolution failure)
signature: temporary failure resolving ubuntu archive mirror hosts during apt get update package has no installation candidate|Network

failed_jobs.name: Debian Packages / Debian Packages
failed_jobs.symptom: apt-get install/update fails: DNS resolution of Ubuntu archive mirrors (azure.archive.ubuntu.com, archive.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com) times out

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_24
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check fails because the Debian Packages job failed

key_errors:
Err:2 http://azure.archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease
  Temporary failure resolving 'azure.archive.ubuntu.com'

Err:3 http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble InRelease

E: Package 'gnupg' has no installation candidate

root_cause: The 'Install debian packages & check conflicts' step runs `apt-get update` to refresh package indices before installing gnupg/wget/ca-certificates/lsb-release and the local OpenVINO .deb package. DNS resolution for all configured Ubuntu mirror hostnames (azure.archive.ubuntu.com, archive.ubuntu.com, security.ubuntu.com) failed with 'Temporary failure resolving' inside the job's container/runner network, so apt could not fetch any index files and subsequently reported the referenced packages as having no installation candidate. This is a transient DNS/network outage affecting the runner or its network path to the Ubuntu mirrors, not a problem with the PR's code changes (which only touch NPU compiler-adapter C++ sources unrelated to packaging).
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible locally; requires the same runner network/DNS outage. To reproduce conceptually: run `apt-get update` in the same Docker image used by the Debian Packages job while DNS resolution to archive.ubuntu.com/azure.archive.ubuntu.com is blocked or failing.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job once DNS/network connectivity recovers (handled automatically via remediate_transient_failure for this run)
Consider adding retry/backoff logic around `apt-get update` in the Debian Packages workflow step to tolerate transient mirror DNS failures
If this failure continues recurring at high frequency, escalate to infrastructure/runner team to investigate DNS resolver health on the affected runner pool
prevention_strategies: Add a retry loop (e.g., 3 attempts with backoff) around `apt-get update` / `apt-get install` in the Debian Packages job definition so transient DNS blips do not fail the whole job. Consider pinning a secondary/fallback mirror or using an internal apt cache/proxy to reduce dependency on public Ubuntu mirror DNS resolution.
historical_context: This exact signature has now recurred 8 times, most within the last several hours (prior runs: 43056188729, 43056184381, 43049573225, 43046960596, 43040586954, 43040586616, 43030484756), consistently categorized as Network/DNS failures against Ubuntu apt mirrors. A rerun-pattern PR (#39740) proposing the search string 'Temporary failure resolving' is already open and pending maintainer review for this exact signature.
